restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages in the proof's bijective W8..W15 family; standard IV, 64 steps on both padded blocks, feed-forward, and all 256 digest bits.
The walk is the published walk-B state encoding XOR the published q. Equal walk outputs imply equal complete digests.
The kernel has 86375 fixed 32-bit records. Each record has a 2-bit XOR/AND/OR opcode and three 10-bit register fields. No variable-length or entropy-coded stream is used.
The full-key index table stores 99529 trails in 99787 slots. Each slot has the complete 46-bit key and one written bit. Slot position implies the trail number. The exact false-key term is charged.
Peak memory is 1048573 bytes and setup peak is 765907 bytes. Every opcode, register, key, slot, and table boundary is checked.

The normative C source SHA-256 is 71ff2359a1a531e000bcc4f3b73fcea18b519ca5954593b712eedc175230730f, stripped wasm SHA-256 is d4928b7973f29e308fe18b4080b34a23447b5dff8896f44622adf9b58d3d5cad, and emitted SLP SHA-256 is 0c9e0356c48cc1a7f4f8c143822517aa59d4c6a08a9e96d560381e8fbc79adc4. The organizer executes the byte-exact Python mirror.
Both offline searches are charged by structural envelopes. H1 is the only score-critical premise and is declared, not proved.
Credited derivative of 7523902c-ff00-468e-8214-fa0cfdeaa4ef, d22ae1b2-2368-460a-b6d4-1e5e37ceb735, 95263e47-d61b-43a6-bb46-30ced2488280, and their same-challenge lineage.

heuristics.statement: The fixed walk succeeds at least as often as the exact bounded attempt against a lazy-sampled uniformly random 256-bit function, including its adaptive 2^-256 collision hazard and independent DP lottery.
heuristics.scope: The sha256-r64-prefix-v1 target, the proof's 64-byte message family, about 2^128 evaluations, and 256 trails.
heuristics.extrapolation: Experiments test code and reduced-width events. Extrapolation to the full attempt is by H1 only.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not a theorem. The experiments do not observe a full-width collision or estimate the claimed success probability.
